page: Microsoft Azure F16ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 4.5 GHz, operating with one execution thread per core under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration includes 64 GB of system memory, yielding 4 GB of memory per core, paired with a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe solid-state drive for high-speed temporary storage. No discrete GPU acceleration is included in this hardware profile.

Benchmark testing reveals high single-threaded compute efficiency, driven by the 4.5 GHz clock frequency and AMD Zen-based architecture with AVX-512 instruction extensions such as VNNI and BF16. Geekbench single-core results and stress-ng single-core tests place the instance in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Compression and decompression benchmarks show strong performance, specifically in single-threaded gzip and bzip3 throughput. Multi-core performance is robust across compilation and text processing tasks, while broader multi-core benchmarks align with mid-tier results across the 16-core category.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated core allocation ensures predictable CPU execution without multi-threading contention. The integrated NVMe SSD eliminates network transfer overhead for IO-heavy scratch workloads, though instances using local storage require external durability strategies for persistent state. The 1:4 core-to-memory ratio provides balanced resource utilization for compute-centric applications without incurring the premium of high-memory tiers. The F16ads_v7 is suitable for software compilation pipelines, batch data processing, web serving, and database tasks requiring fast local scratch disks.
